details.description: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3 is Mistral AI's third instruction-tuned release of Mistral 7B, published in May 2024. It is a 7.24-billion-parameter dense transformer that, per its Hugging Face model card, extends the vocabulary to 32,768 tokens with Mistral's v3 tokenizer and adds native function-calling support not present in v0.1 or v0.2. It supports a 32,768-token context length and is released under the Apache 2.0 license. Mistral AI's models overview lists Mistral 7B Instruct as deprecated and replaced by Ministral 3 8B, and lists Mistral 7B (v0.1-v0.3) with a deprecation date of November 30, 2024 and a retirement date of March 30, 2025.
advantages: Adds native function-calling support, unlike Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1 and v0.2, per its Hugging Face model card.
Supports a 32,768-token context length with an extended v3 tokenizer vocabulary, per its Hugging Face model card.
Released under the Apache 2.0 license, permitting commercial use.
disadvantages: Mistral states the model has no built-in moderation mechanisms.

Mistral AI's models overview (docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/models/) lists Mistral 7B Instruct as deprecated and replaced by Ministral 3 8B, and lists Mistral 7B (v0.1-v0.3) with a deprecation date of November 30, 2024 and a retirement date of March 30, 2025.
use_cases: Conversational chat and instruction-following with tool/function calling
Agentic systems and structured prompt generation, per Fireworks' model page

notes: Catalog facts list max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens of 32768 with no deprecation_date, matching both the model's 32,768-token vocabulary/context figure and Fireworks' host page. No evaluation table was found on the Hugging Face page across repeat fetches, so evaluations was left empty. Mistral's own docs state the v0.1-v0.3 line is deprecated (11/30/2024) and retired (3/30/2025), which the catalog's empty deprecation_date does not reflect. Verify pass: the 'agentic systems and structured prompt generation' use case is not on the Hugging Face card (checked again); it is stated on Fireworks' model page for this id, already in sources, so the attribution was corrected to that page rather than removing the claim.
